Playbook.name: Windows — Executable or Script Written to an Administrative Share (Lateral Tool Transfer) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An executable or script was written to an administrative share (C$/ADMIN$) via SMB (5145 with WriteData to an .exe/.dll/.ps1/etc.). Triage question: is this an attacker staging a tool for remote execution (lateral movement), or a legitimate software-deployment/admin action?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Writing a binary to a remote admin share is the staging step of PsExec-style lateral movement - a tool is placed before it is run remotely.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Destination host (where the file was written).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the file write to the admin share is lateral-movement tool staging or a legitimate deployment.

Step.name: What was written, from where, by whom
Step.Purpose: The file name/type, source and account reveal tool-staging vs software deployment.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "5145" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND winlog.event_data.ShareName LIKE "*$" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | KEEP @timestamp, src, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.ShareName, winlog.event_data.RelativeTargetName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: A randomly-named .exe written to ADMIN$ from a workstation = tool staging. A signed installer to C$ from a deployment server = software push. Note the source and account.

Step.name: Was a remote service/task then created on this host (execution)
Step.Purpose: Tool staging followed by remote service/task creation is the PsExec lateral-execution chain completing.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-*,logs-system.system-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("7045","4697","4698") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.ServiceName, winlog.event_data.ServiceFileName, winlog.event_data.TaskName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A new service/task referencing the just-written file right after the write confirms lateral execution - escalate to IR. Empty = staging only (still investigate).

Node.Condition: A tool/binary written to an admin share from a workstation/unexpected source, especially followed by remote service/task creation.
Node.Result: True Positive (Lateral Tool Transfer / Remote Exec - IR)

Node.Condition: A signed software package pushed by a documented deployment system.
Admin manually copying a legitimate tool for a known task.
Write from an unclear source with no follow-on.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-ADMSHARE-WRITE, INV-02-ADMSHARE-EXEC to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Legitimate software deployment or admin file copy.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the deployment; close as false_positive/benign_activity.

TruePositive.Definition: Lateral-movement tool staging for remote execution.

Indicators.Item: Random/unsigned binary to an admin share.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate source and destination; open IR; remove the staged tool.
Reset credentials used; hunt the source's other targets.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A backup/sync tool writing executables to shares by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
